newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto may reject election results, party sources.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto may reject election results, party sources.

text.p: Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, heading for a crushing defeat in Pakistan's national and provincial assembly elections, may reject the results, party sources said on Tuesday.

The sources, speaking at her home in the village of Naudero in the southern province of Sindh, said Bhutto would hold a meeting of leaders of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP) in Islamabad on Wednesday to decide the party's strategy.

With 63 results declared for the 217-seat National Assembly (lower house), the PPP had won only three seats, against 46 for the Pakistan Muslim League (PML) led by Bhutto's main rival and former prime minister Nawaz Sharif.
The PPP sources, who asked not to be named, said the party felt there had been widespread rigging and irregularities, and might decide to boycott the national and provincial assemblies.

An air of gloom settled over Bhutto's farmhouse at Naudero as results broadcast on state television showed the extent of the electoral disaster for the PPP. "It's unbelievable, just unbelievable," muttered one party official.

President Farooq Leghari called the elections after sacking Bhutto's government on November 5, citing corruption, nepotism and other abuses. Bhutto, who was due to leave Naudero for Islamabad later on Tuesday, denies the charges.
